rungs.summary: The foundation: the app runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, asks you to accept its licence, and scrolls a script with the character-based engine from Freally Capture.
The standalone teleprompter: a script library, pause chips, a projector for the talent with a mirror flip, a mirror to phones on your own network, a real transport, BPM pacing and read-aloud.
Offline autocomplete: it finishes words and common phrases as you type, in all 18 languages, from word lists inside the app.
The first full release: a one-minute welcome tour, a keyboard and screen-reader pass, a theme that follows your system, and updates that install only after you say yes.
Write your script by speaking: dictation that runs on your computer, with nothing to train.
Dictation, finished: a proper record button, words that land where your cursor is, and an undo that takes back one thing you said.
Reading to time: a tempo you tap to match your delivery, a metronome, a bar and beat counter, rehearsal with a timing report, and labels that cost no read time.
Getting the script in: import Word, RTF, PDF, text and Markdown files, section markers with a jump list, find and replace, and script statistics.
Anything in the room can drive it: foot pedals and presenter remotes, keys that work when the app is not in front, and a rebindable map of every command.
Built for the rig: a vertical flip for overhead glass, lens and safe-margin guides, an elapsed and remaining time display, and presets for reading at a distance.
Never lose a take: recovery of unsaved edits after a crash, settings that travel with each script, local version history, and export to PDF for a paper backup.
Help with the writing: a rhyme finder, syllable counts for each line, a tongue-twister check and suggested pauses — from dictionaries, with no model.
Drive it from anywhere: a phone-sized control page, plus MIDI and OSC for the desk you already run — on your own network only, and off by default.
Run a whole show: rundowns with a duration for each item, more than one prompter output, and a big countdown and cue-light display for the floor.
Record while you prompt: a webcam take as the script runs, or audio only with your section markers written into the file as chapters.
Every script, every language: emphasis on single words, furigana above the line, right-to-left polish for Arabic, and vertical Japanese and Chinese.
Version 2.0: all of the above, on Windows, macOS and Linux.
